claim: CMC provides atoms, journaling, and bitemporal preservation.
CMC implementation artifacts exist and are validated by tests.
Provenance and snapshots enable recovery and auditing.
Hash-chained journal segments protect integrity and enable quarantine.
Bitemporal queries must support both transaction-time and valid-time replays.
CMC consists of five core components: Memory Store, Bitemporal Engine, Provenance/Witness Store, Snapshot Manager, and API/Schema Layer.
Write path includes seven stages: Ingest → Atomize → Enrich → Index (HHNI) → Gate → Persist → Snapshot.
Read path includes: HHNI Lookup → DVNS Physics → Deduplication → Conflict Resolution → Compression.
CMC integrates with HHNI for hierarchical indexing, VIF for witness storage, SEG for provenance graphs, APOE for context retrieval, and SDF-CVF for quartet parity.
Atom schema includes identity (UUID), modality, content reference, embedding, tags, TPV, temporal fields, and VIF witness envelope.
Snapshot restore procedure (create, verify, execute, restore, replay) is codified for Wave 1.
SnapshotManager APIs in advanced_pipelines.py back the runnable examples for logging integrity reports.
Tier S gate policy enforces vif_min and intelligent metric thresholds for CMC work.
READY_TO_EXECUTE.md defines the Wave 1 sequencing that CMC atoms refer to.
